title: Prague in 3 days: a winter itinerary
author: Brogan
intro: Three days is a good amount of time for Prague. You can see the castle, the Old Town and Charles Bridge, and still have time for the Christmas markets, a beer hall and a quieter corner or two. Here's a plan that works well in winter.
seo_description: 3 days is about right: the castle and Lesser Town, the Old Town and Jewish Quarter, and Vyšehrad, plus the Christmas markets from 28 November 2026.

sections.heading: Is 3 days enough for Prague?
sections.text:
Yes. Prague's centre is compact, and most of the main sights are within walking distance of each other. Three full days gives you time to see the big ones without rushing, and to enjoy the city's cafés and beer halls.

In winter, the days are short: it gets dark at about 4pm in December. That's no bad thing in Prague, as the Old Town and the castle look wonderful lit up at night. Just plan to see the outdoor sights in the morning and early afternoon.

The Christmas market on **Old Town Square** is expected to run from **28 November 2026 to 6 January 2027**, with smaller markets around the city.

sections.heading: Day 1: the Old Town and Charles Bridge
sections.text:
Start at **Old Town Square**, with its pastel houses, the Gothic **Týn Church** and the **Astronomical Clock** on the Old Town Hall. The clock's figures move on the hour, and crowds gather to watch. Climb the town hall tower for the view over the rooftops.

After lunch, walk through **Josefov**, the old Jewish Quarter. Its synagogues and the **Old Jewish Cemetery** are some of the most moving places in the city, and are visited on a combined ticket.

In the late afternoon, cross **Charles Bridge** as the lights come on, then come back for the Christmas market on Old Town Square in the evening. Try **trdelník**, a sweet pastry roll, or a hot **svařák**, Czech mulled wine.

sections.heading: Day 2: Prague Castle and the Lesser Town
sections.text:
Get to **Prague Castle** early, as it's busiest from late morning. It's one of the largest castle complexes in the world, with **St Vitus Cathedral**, the Old Royal Palace and **Golden Lane**, a row of tiny colourful houses. A circuit ticket covers the main buildings.

Walk down through the **Lesser Town** (Malá Strana), with its baroque palaces and the green-domed **St Nicholas Church**. If it's clear, climb **Petřín Hill**, or take the funicular when it's running, for one of the best views of Prague.

End the day in a traditional beer hall. Czech beer is famous and good value, and hearty dishes like goulash with dumplings are perfect in winter.

sections.heading: Day 3: Vyšehrad and the New Town
sections.text:
Take the metro or tram south to **Vyšehrad**, an old fortress on a cliff above the river. It's much quieter than the castle, with lovely views back towards the city, the twin-spired **Basilica of St Peter and St Paul** and a cemetery where the composers Dvořák and Smetana are buried.

In the afternoon, head to **Wenceslas Square** in the New Town, which also has a Christmas market, and visit the **Dancing House** on the riverbank. If it's very cold, spend the afternoon in a museum or café: Prague's grand old cafés, like **Café Louvre**, are perfect for warming up.

In the evening, watch the sunset from the riverbank or take an evening cruise on the Vltava.

sections.heading: Tips for Prague in winter
sections.text:
- **Pack for the cold.** December highs are around 2 to 3°C, and it's often below freezing at night. Bring good shoes for icy cobbles.
- **Go early or late.** Charles Bridge and the castle are far quieter before about 9am.
- **Pay in koruna.** The Czech Republic uses the Czech koruna, not the euro. Cards are widely accepted, but avoid exchange booths with poor rates, and say no to paying in pounds when using a card.
- **Use public transport.** Trams and the metro are cheap and easy, and a 24-hour or 72-hour ticket covers both.
- **Book the busiest weekends early.** Hotel prices rise sharply in the run-up to Christmas and at New Year.

sections.heading: Where to stay
sections.text:
For a short trip, stay in or near the **Old Town** (Staré Město) or the **Lesser Town** (Malá Strana). Both put the main sights within walking distance, and it's lovely to walk back through the lit-up streets at night. The Lesser Town is quieter in the evenings and closer to the castle.

The **New Town** (Nové Město), around Wenceslas Square, is a little cheaper and very well connected by metro and tram, though it's busier and less charming. **Vinohrady**, just to the south-east, is a leafy residential area with good cafés and restaurants, and it's a short tram ride into the centre.

In December, the most central hotels fill up early, especially at weekends, so book as soon as you know your dates.

sections.heading: Getting there
sections.text:
Prague has lots of direct flights from the UK, and the flight takes about two hours from London. From the airport, buses connect to the metro, or the Airport Express bus runs to the main railway station. A taxi to the centre takes about 30 minutes.

Prague is one hour ahead of the UK.

sections.heading: Prague or somewhere else?
sections.text:
If you're weighing up Prague against other Christmas cities, read [Vienna or Prague at Christmas](/blog/vienna-or-prague-at-christmas) and our list of the [best Christmas markets in Europe](/blog/best-christmas-markets-in-europe). For good-value alternatives, try [Budapest](/destinations/budapest), [Kraków](/destinations/krakow) or [Riga](/destinations/riga). Our [Riga Christmas market 2026](/blog/riga-christmas-market-2026) post has the dates.

Our [Prague guide](/destinations/prague) covers when to go and what to see in other seasons. For more festive ideas, see our [Christmas holidays](/destinations/christmas-holidays) page, and for other short trips, see the [best places for a 3-day city break in Europe](/blog/best-places-for-a-3-day-city-break-in-europe).

faqs.question: Is 3 days enough in Prague?
faqs.answer: Yes. Three full days is enough for the Old Town, Charles Bridge, the castle, the Lesser Town and a quieter area like Vyšehrad.

faqs.question: When are the Prague Christmas markets in 2026?
faqs.answer: The main market on Old Town Square is expected to run from 28 November 2026 to 6 January 2027. Wenceslas Square and other squares have smaller markets.

faqs.question: Is Prague cold in December?
faqs.answer: Yes. Highs are around 2 to 3°C, and nights are often below freezing. Snow is possible but not guaranteed.

faqs.question: What currency does Prague use?
faqs.answer: The Czech koruna (CZK). Cards are widely accepted, but it's useful to carry a little cash for market stalls.
